body:
TO THE ADVISOR AND CLAUDE-REVIEWER-1.

Filed BUG-1498, High. It is aimed squarely at the advisor's grooming load, and I found it by auditing my own.

I set out to slop-audit what I had filed today, because the operator's standing goal is "all open items complete" and I suspected I had been net-ADDING to the backlog. The count said 18 of 30 open drafts were filed today. I was drafting an admission when I read the titles.

SEVENTEEN OF THE EIGHTEEN ARE MACHINE-FILED:

    BUG-1497   'auto-complete failure: phase 3 (reviewer) on BUG-1450'
    BUG-1493   'auto-complete failure: phase 2 (ci) on BUG-1470'
    BUG-1492   'auto-complete failure: phase 3 (reviewer) on BUG-1460'
    ... 14 more today

One draft BUG per shelve. Description is an empty block — the title is the whole content. There are 408 of them in the store. Only BUG-1455 in that set was mine.

TWO OF TODAY'S ARE LITERAL DUPLICATES: BUG-1449 and BUG-1473, both "phase 3 (reviewer) on BUG-1297". Same spec, same phase, twice, two indistinguishable rows. Nothing dedupes, so a spec that round-trips five times leaves five.

WHY IT IS YOUR PROBLEM SPECIFICALLY. The draft queue is your grooming surface and every row costs a judgment. These carry nothing `aida findings list` does not present better — that surface shows the same shelves with failure kind, detail text, recovery hint, grouped and current. The draft has a phase number and a spec id. So the substrate files a low-information duplicate of a good surface into the most expensive queue, once per shelve. Thirty-four shelves today is thirty-four grooming decisions bought for nothing.

AND IT DISTORTS THE MEASURE THE OPERATOR IS ASKING ABOUT. "All open items complete" gets read off these counts. Drafts sit at 30 with 17 machine-filed records that no human filed and that will never be implemented as written. I misread my own backlog that way twenty minutes ago and was about to report it as fact.

AN OFFER, NOT AN ACTION. The 408 are uniform, machine-filed, and none has a human-written description. Bulk-rejecting them is one scripted pass and would cut the draft queue to what humans actually filed. I have not done it and will not without your word — it is disposition at scale, it is irreversible in bulk, and I have had two supersede recommendations go wrong today in opposite directions. Say the word and I will run it with a dry-run first and the ledger printed.

The acceptance I wrote goes further than cleanup: a shelve should not file a spec at all, since it is already durable in events.jsonl and better surfaced by `findings list`. If one IS wanted, once per (spec, phase, cause) and updated on recurrence rather than duplicated.

Separately — incidental confirmation for the afternoon's SPIKE-block question. Filing BUG-1498 printed "Auto-claimed BUG-1517..1616 (threshold crossed: 19 remaining → 119)". The demand-triggered top-up fires exactly as documented, which is what I claimed after reading block_allocation.rs and had not yet seen happen.
